description: The rule of the batcher (REQ-DLV-006): a batch leaves when it holds batch_size events or when the oldest event waiting is flush_interval_ms old, whichever comes first; one worker sends one batch at a time, each send takes send_duration_ms, and the order is kept. The expected batches are computed by an independent model (see the algorithm). plan(now, queued, oldest_arrival, batch_size, flush_interval_ms) answers: idle when queued is 0 (wait for ever); send with take = batch_size when queued >= batch_size; send with take = min(queued, batch_size) when now - oldest_arrival >= flush_interval_ms; otherwise wait for oldest_arrival + flush_interval_ms - now. The algorithm of the simulation, with a clock that moves only to the next arrival or the next decision: now = 0, free_at = 0; loop: push every event whose at <= now; if now >= free_at: ask plan; on send, take the events, record a batch {at_ms: now, ids}, set free_at = now + send_duration_ms and loop again WITHOUT moving the clock; on wait, next_decision = now + wait_ms; on idle, next_decision is never; if now < free_at, next_decision = free_at; next_arrival is the at of the next event not yet pushed; move now to the smaller of the two and stop when both are never. ids are 1-based in the order of arrivals. The queue is unbounded here: the limit and the drop policy are T-05.2.

cases.name: five_events_wait_for_the_interval
cases.description: A batch that is not full leaves when the oldest event is flush_interval_ms old.

cases.name: a_full_batch_leaves_at_once
cases.description: A batch that reaches batch_size leaves at the moment it is full, not at the interval.

cases.name: two_hundred_and_fifty_at_once
cases.description: 250 events at the same time with batch 100: two full batches at once and the rest at the interval.

cases.name: the_interval_counts_from_the_oldest_event
cases.description: The second batch is timed from the arrival of the oldest event that is left, not from the last send.

cases.name: the_boundary_is_inclusive
cases.description: An event that is exactly flush_interval_ms old is sent.

cases.name: a_batch_of_one
cases.description: With batch_size 1 every event leaves at once.

cases.name: a_slow_destination_delays_only_the_next_batch
cases.description: While a send takes 500 ms the worker sends nothing else: the next batch leaves when the worker is free, and the order is kept.

cases.name: a_busy_worker_and_an_old_event
cases.description: An event that waited while the worker was busy is sent as soon as the worker is free.
